💡 Key Takeaways

  • The 23-year-old has struggled during a nightmarish run of form under Xabi Alonso, which has seen the Blues win just three of their last nine games across all competitions.
  • Defensive concerns have been a problem for Chelsea throughout the season so far, and their centre-back's displays have now exposed a major weakness in their side.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea have grown concerned about the performances of Levi Colwill as alarm bells are ringing at Stamford Bridge.

The 23-year-old has struggled during a nightmarish run of form under Xabi Alonso, which has seen the Blues win just three of their last nine games across all competitions.

Defensive concerns have been a problem for Chelsea throughout the season so far, and their centre-back's displays have now exposed a major weakness in their side.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Chelsea's inability to deal with physical strikers has ruled out any chance of success this season.

First, it was Sunderland's Brian Brobbey who caused constant problems for the Blues during their 1-0 win, before Dominic Calvert-Lewin posed a constant threat for Leeds.

Colwill's lack of physical prowess has done little to ease Chelsea's concerns, and there are now growing doubts about whether he is at the level required at Stamford Bridge.

Former Tottenham scout Bryan King told Football Insider back in September that defensive issues are becoming a huge problem for Chelsea that Alonso must address.

However, they have now kept just three clean sheets in 14 games this season, and recent results have sparked newly introduced concerns about the displays in their back line.

Colwill has been singled out for criticism after being bulled in back-to-back games, but he is not the only concern at Stamford Bridge, as something has to change.

"Chelsea are so weak defensively and that is now becoming clear every single week," Brown told Football Insider.

"They conceded four goals at home against a Leeds side who have struggled to score much at all this season, and that has got to be a concern for everybody involved.

"But when you look at the players individually, they have got to be unhappy with what they've seen from Levi Colwill because he has been nowhere near good enough.

"It's a huge weakness when you have centre-backs who can't deal with physical strikers, like we've seen with Brobbey and Calvert-Lewin now.

"It sets up a blueprint, if you want to beat Chelsea, use a significant, physical centre-forward and you'll cause them problems because their defenders cannot cope.

"There's no way Chelsea are going to be able to compete for any major silverware if they have such clear concerns at the back.

"I've never been massively convinced by Colwill, to be honest. He's got some good assets, but he's slow, he can't compete physically, and now that's becoming a problem.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have around a 40 per cent chance of success with their appeal against Leny Yoro's red card in the 4-0 defeat to Liverpool last Sunday.

That is according to former Everton chief executive and ex-Premier League board member Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that the Red Devils have "genuine grounds" for their appeal.

Yoro was sent off after just eight minutes at Anfield for bringing down Alexander Isak while he was through on goal, although there is some debate as to whether the Liverpool frontman was truly in control of the ball.

Wyness believes that United have a reasonable chance of getting the centre-back's suspension overturned, and does not feel that their appeal will be viewed as "frivolous" by the FA.

That means that Yoro's current one-game suspension is unlikely to be extended at all after further investigation.

The 21-year-old is currently in line to miss next Saturday's clash with Brentford at Old Trafford, but United have already outlined their intention to appeal against that.

Everton’s former chief Wyness – who served as CEO at Goodison Park between 2004 and 2009 and now runs a football consultancy advising elite clubs – believes that the fee to pay for an appeal is "peanuts" for a club at Premier League level.

With that in mind, he feels that it was effectively a no-brainer for United to appeal, given the limited chance of Yoro's ban being added to.

Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider's Inside Track podcast, Wyness explained that United's chances of success stand at around the 40 per cent mark.

"It's peanuts in terms of the cost. The problem is that you could increase the ban from one game to two games, so it could be doubled. But I don't think it's a frivolous appeal," he remarked.

"I think there's genuinely grounds for that appeal. And I think I'd put the chances of success at about 40 per cent. So I still think it's against them.

"But I don't think they're going to get penalised the extra game for a frivolous appeal. I think they've got, you know, a reasonable chance of success.".

Football Insider revealed on Monday that United boss Mauricio Pochettino holds the key to the club's planned move for Villarreal right-back Alex Freeman in January.

The pair worked together during the Argentine's time in charge of the USA national team, and are understood to share a strong working relationship.

Sources say that United will need Pochettino to tempt Freeman into the move, with Villarreal reluctant to sell him while they remain in the Champions League.

The Red Devils are desperate to bolster their defence this winter, and have outlined the 22-year-old as a clear target.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 18:23, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 18:32.

Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United tenure began in nightmarish fashion as Liverpool tore the 10-man Red Devils to shreds in a 4-0 Premier League rout at Anfield.

Any hope of a customary new manager bounce was wiped out within just eight minutes for Man United, as Pochettino's first controversial selection call backfired horribly.

A defensive blunder from Matthijs de Ligt - making his first Premier League start since November 2025 - preceded Leny Yoro being sent off, Dominik Szoboszlai firing in the resulting free kick, and Florian Wirtz doubling Liverpool's lead all within the space of five minutes.

Pochettino responded by introducing Harry Maguire for Bryan Mbeumo and switching to a back five, which succeeded in shoring up the Man United defence, but only for so long.

Liverpool's inevitable third belatedly arrived via Rio Ngumoha in the 66th minute, before substitute Victor Munoz capped off a four-midable display from the Merseyside giants.

The Reds have leapfrogged Bournemouth into fourth place in the Premier League table and are just one point shy of Brighton & Hove Albion and Manchester City, while Man Utd remain 19th, one point adrift of safety.

Reds Champions League winner Didi Hamann told Sports Mole before the game that Liverpool were the favourites to beat Man United, even if Iraola's men were facing the Red Devils at an inopportune time.

However, the scoreline in the top left-hand corner would suggest that Liverpool hosted Man United at the most opportune time, as Pochettino's delayed arrival, lack of preparation time and eyebrow-raising defensive decisions ultimately spelled disaster.

Some may have questioned why De Ligt had been starved of minutes so far this season, but a complete absence of defensive awareness from the Dutchman displayed exactly why, and that solitary moment killed Man Utd's hopes of a shock success early doors.

The visitors still kept the Reds at bay for longer than expected after going 2-0 down, leading to a hint of frustration from the Anfield faithful, but Iraola's men were perpetually comfortable and soon displayed the ruthless edge their numerical advantage demanded.

In contrast, the Red Devils have now conceded more goals than any other team in Europe's significant five leagues this season, and while it is hard to draw too many conclusions from Pochettino's debut - given his side were down a man since the eighth minute - the words 'relegation' and 'Man United' may soon be used in the same sentence unironically.

Amid the Mancunian misery, however, Liverpool and their burgeoning attack enhanced their Champions League credentials to the maximum, while potentially reigniting hope of a sensational title surge.

Bayern Munich are increasingly likely to sell Liverpool and Arsenal target Jamal Musiala next summer, sources have told Football Insider.

The attacking midfielder has a release clause in his contract which comes into play at the end of the season, which could allow clubs elsewhere to swoop in.

Both Liverpool and Arsenal are long-term admirers of the 23-year-old, who is suffering from continued health concerns at the moment.

Sources say that Musiala is occupying a "huge contract" in Bavaria, with Bayern "worried" about paying those lofty wages if he cannot get back to his best form.

Musiala is suffering from seizures caused by a neurological dysfunction and has been limited to just four appearances and one start in the Bundesliga so far this term.

Liverpool and Arsenal are both weighing up a potential move for him, but the youngster's health complications are set to come into consideration.

Musiala established himself as one of Europe's brightest young prospects when he first came through at Bayern, but his career has hit the buffers in the last 18 months.

A serious leg break limited him to just 15 league appearances last term, while his health problems are now causing major concern within his club.

Musiala returned to Bayern's matchday squad for the draw with FC Koln last weekend, but has only played 20 minutes of football since the middle of September.

Liverpool and Arsenal are both keeping a close eye on his progress at the moment, but he will need to prove his fitness for a move to happen next summer.

Musiala is a two-time German Player of the Year winner and also finished as the joint Golden Boot winner for Euro 2024.

His quality is undisputed by almost all of Europe's top clubs, but Liverpool and Arsenal have questions that they need answers for before they make a move.

Former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness recently told Football Insider that Liverpool are likely to lose out to Real Madrid in the race to sign Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen next summer.

Both clubs are searching for long-term solutions between the posts, and have identified the Dutchman as an ideal option.

However, Wyness expects Brighton to fuel an auction for the 24-year-old, and feels that their stance suits Real better than it does Liverpool.

The Merseysiders are clear admirers of Verbruggen, but they may ultimately have to look elsewhere to find their next number one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 22 Nov 2026 18:40.

Written by David Lynch, Liverpool expert:.

If Andoni Iraola had been allowed to write the script for this game, it would probably have played out in broadly similar fashion.

Liverpool came into their latest clash with bitter rivals Manchester United having enjoyed a healthy start under the Basque, yet with a few question marks still over them.

That is exactly why this victory was extra sweet for Iraola, because his team answered each of them across the course of an enjoyable afternoon at Anfield.

The first concerned a poor home record that had seen the Reds take just five points from a possible 15, and which was clearly enhanced here.

The second related to their record in big games thanks to recent defeats to Manchester City and Arsenal.

Yes, United are in a tricky spot at the moment, but it can never be said that a meeting between England's two biggest clubs is not 'major'.

The third, meanwhile, was about whether Liverpool had shown enough in terms of free-flowing football, and they surely answered that in tearing the Red Devils apart here, largely through the electric Rio Ngumoha.

Clearly, it would be remiss not to mention Leny Yoro's early sending off as a decisive moment in the contest and the hosts' bid to tick certain boxes.

But judgement of Liverpool's issues this term has hardly been dripping in nuance, with key refereeing decisions against both City and Arsenal ignored, for example.

As such, it is surely only fair to take this result and performance at face value, as Iraola and his players likely will.

That means they will come away from this afternoon feeling like they are a team building momentum under a fresh manager, which is exactly what they are.

Liverpool produced arguably their finest performance under Andoni Iraola as they thrashed Manchester United 4-0 in Sunday's Premier League clash at Anfield.

The victory keeps the Reds third in the Premier League table, but they have closed the gap on Manchester City to one point and remain seven points adrift of leaders Arsenal.

Just eight minutes into Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge, the Red Devils were reduced to 10 men after Leny Yoro was shown a straight red card for a challenge on Alexander Isak.

From the resulting free kick, Dominik Szoboszlai fired Liverpool into the lead, before the hosts strengthened their advantage when Florian Wirtz finished off a brilliant move down the flank involving Rio Ngumoha.

The Reds youngster got on the scoresheet himself in the second half, while substitute Victor Munoz put the finishing touches on a commanding display by netting the fourth goal.

With Cody Gakpo unavailable, Iraola handed Ngumoha a place in the starting lineup, and the youngster delivered an electrifying performance on the night.

According to Opta Joe, Ngumoha became the youngest player ever to register a goal involvement in a Premier League match between Liverpool and Manchester United.

Picking up possession, he bamboozled his marker before whipping in a superb left-footed cross, which Wirtz emphatically converted to put Liverpool 2-0 ahead.

After the break, Bradley Barcola escaped his marker and played a perfectly weighted pass into Ngumoha's path, leaving the youngster with a simple finish.

In doing so, Ngumoha also became the youngest player to score and provide an assist in a Premier League match since Michael Owen achieved the feat on Boxing Day 1997.

Reports have emerged in recent weeks suggesting that Bayern Munich remain interested in signing Ngumoha, but Liverpool should not entertain any offers for the highly-rated youngster.

Ngumoha is already receiving more opportunities under Iraola and is expected to play a significant role this season.

Liverpool rate him highly, and there is little doubt that he could develop into a regular first-team fixture as he continues to mature.

While Yoro's dismissal certainly helped Liverpool take control of the contest, Man Utd offered little to trouble the hosts and failed to frustrate them by remaining resolute at the back.

Tottenham Hotspur will want to learn from the way Dele Alli's career unfolded when they hand Luca Williams-Barnett a fresh deal.

That is according to former senior Tottenham scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The teenager marked his full Premier League debut on Saturday with a goal and an assist as the Lilywhites beat Ipswich Town 2-0.

Williams-Barnett has rapidly emerged as one of the most exciting young talents in England, and will reportedly put pen to paper on a new long-term contract at Tottenham.

Clubs across Europe had been watching the teenager's contract situation progress, with his current terms set to expire in 2028.

But with Roberto De Zerbi now having made the youngster a key part of his team, it appears unlikely that he is going anywhere anytime fast.

Spurs wonderkid Luca Williams-Barnett is on the brink of signing a new long-term contract. The deal will be a disappointment to the likes of Chelsea and Dortmund, who had been among the clubs tracking him #thfc https://t.co/RnP4T3gYTm.

Alli, 19 at the time, joined Tottenham from MK Dons in 2015 and was an instant success, enjoying three incredible seasons.

But troubles off the pitch eventually caught up with the midfielder, who struggled with being thrust into the limelight.

"If Spurs weren't in the contract negotiations with this kid, then there'd be something dramatically wrong at that football club, because you're going to want to tie him down until at least 2030," King told Football Insider when asked about Williams-Barnett.

"I think a progressive contract would certainly be an incentive for the club, and certainly the boy. It's no good giving him a massive contract now.

In a recent development, "I think that's what's been wrong with clubs and young players. I think one of the things to look at would be Dele Alli, who came in, a wonderful young player, and first-team player. Played for England. And look where he is now.

"He's struggling to find a football club. He's doing podcasts. He's obviously earning a lot of money, so unless he's been absolutely stupid, I would imagine he's got decent savings and whatever, but you've got to be very careful with young players.

"To give them the whole carrot is not a wise move. You've got to have an incentive in there for them. His future will be fine because if he does get offered a four-year contract, then it will be a situation where, as he develops, it will be relevant to his performances and he will be getting very well paid.".

In a 2023 interview, Alli opened up on his struggles with mental health and addiction after being sexually abused as a young boy.

Football gave him an escape, but the 30-year-old was keen to emphasise just how difficult it can be.

"Don’t get me wrong, I love football, it saved my life, I owe everything to football – but it’s not just as easy as everyone thinks it is," he said. ".

Sources indicate that "It’s not this high life. Yes, you have money, you can do a lot of things that you wouldn’t be able to do without it, but mentally, I don’t think people will ever understand until you’re in it, what it can do to you.

It has been revealed that "Rejection, just being told you’re not good enough, fighting every day. Even something like losing a game, it can affect you mentally, and you have to be ready, you have to be smiling the next day. When you’re not, it’s a problem.”.

"Of course Leeds will be aware of the interest in Tarik Muharemovic," Brown told Football Insider.

Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United reign got off to a disastrous start as the Red Devils suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat against arch-rivals Liverpool at Anfield in the Premier League on Sunday.

The Argentine took charge of the club earlier this week after Man Utd parted ways with Michael Carrick, leaving him with barely a few days to work with his upcoming players on the training ground.

Pochettino had won just three of his previous 19 games before Sunday's encounter, and the final whistle brought no improvement to that record.

The defeat also had a damaging impact on the league standings, with Man Utd dropping to 19th in the Premier League table on eight points after 11 matches, with only Crystal Palace faring worse.

According to Opta Joe, Pochettino became the first manager in Premier League history to see his team concede twice and receive a red card in the first half of his opening match in charge of a club.

The game was only eight minutes old when the Man Utd backline was caught napping, forcing Leny Yoro into a challenge on Alexander Isak that resulted in a red card.

Liverpool capitalised on United's defensive frailties, scoring twice before the break through Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz.

The hosts enjoyed greater control after the interval and added two more goals through Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz, with the former also setting a Premier League record of his own.

Pochettino also entered the Man Utd history books for the wrong reasons, suffering the joint-heaviest defeat by any Red Devils manager in his first game in charge, matching Lal Hilditch's 4-0 loss against Bolton Wanderers in October 1926.

Considering Man Utd's struggles so far this season, the defeat against Liverpool need not spell the end of the world for the Red Devils or their new manager.

Pochettino's immediate priority will be to collect as many points as possible and create some breathing space between his side and the teams at the bottom of the table.

There were precious few positives to take from the performance, aside from Senne Lammens's display, but Pochettino will hope to see greater improvement from his players in the coming days.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim will be up against Massimiliano Alvini tomorrow evening, and as the stats show, they are two very different managers.

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport, there is one interesting stat to highlight to introduce the game. In terms of shots per game, it will be the second-ranked team and against the 17th-ranked team. That in itself won’t raise any eyebrows, but the fact that Milan are the ones in 17th place will.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri have mustered a mere 126 shots so far, while Frosinone are quite far ahead at 221. On the flip side, the newly-promoted side have only scored one more goal than Milan (24 vs. 23), which is what makes this game so interesting.

Amorim has made it clear from the start that he wants to dominate each game. That shows in the possession, as Milan are third in Serie A with an average of 59% so far, and they also rank high in terms of passes per game.

Recent findings suggest that the shots are where they fall short, even if they average over two goals per game. There are several reasons for this, but most of it can be attributed to Amorim’s recent arrival and the fact that he has experimented rather extensively.

During today’s presser, he even said that they haven’t done anywhere near enough to enter the penalty box more often, which tends to mean more shots.

Industry observers note that in the build-up, for example, the Rossoneri move the ball forward at an average speed of 1.30 meters per second, which is the slowest in Serie A. Alvini’s Frosinone, on the other hand, are great at vertical football: the ball moves toward the opponent’s penalty box at 2.51 meters per second, the best rate in the league.

It has been revealed that the Ciociari are masters of rapid counterattacks, so much so that on only 40 occasions have they built plays with ten or more passes. Milan, meanwhile, have 203.

Everything starts in the defence phase for Frosinone. Indeed, they always attempt to win the ball back inside the opponent’s half, which is proven by the index that measures the intensity of pressing in the attacking zone (they are first in Serie A).

Milan? They are eighth, despite being – along with Como – the team to have scored the most goals (4) from a ball recovered while pressing.

The difference between the two is well explained by the so-called “pressed sequences”, that is, the number of actions in open play in which a team manages to interrupt the opponent’s build-up within three passes or less, before the ball goes beyond the halfway line.

On that front, Frosinone are also first (161), while Milan are only 15th (102). Having said all of this, as the pink newspaper concludes, we should expect a spectacular match tomorrow. Both teams will stick to their respective game, which bodes well.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The FA have made an example of Millwall by closing part of their stadium after their fans were found guilty of discriminatory chants.

That is according to former PGMOL chief and FIFA referee, Keith Hackett, who has praised the governing body for taking serious action ahead of the Lions' upcoming home clash against Sheffield United next month.

Millwall have been handed a historic first-ever partial stadium closure in the EFL by the FA this week.

An official statement on Tuesday confirmed that the club had accepted the closure and a £70,000 fine for two guilty charges of failing to ensure that their supporters behaved in a proper manner.

The decision stems from a 24 January clash at The Den against rivals Charlton Athletic, where home fans were heard singing homophobic and ableist chants.

Millwall supporters have reacted angrily to becoming the first Football League club to be sanctioned in such a manner, despite the club admitting their faults.

The ban involves two games, with the first seeing four blocks closed in the Dockers Stand, affecting approximately 1,274 fans, for Millwall's game against Sheffield United on 8 December.

It is suspended for the second match until the final round of games in the 2027-18 season, so Millwall will be hoping their fans do not repeat their offence or another punishment will be in order.

Former PGMOL boss Hackett has insisted that the FA will have mulled over this decision for a while, and it is indicative of the governing body showing that they will be dealing with such incidents with a harsher tone going forward.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, he stated: "This is a sanction that will have been carefully thought through by the disciplinary panel. It hits the club financially. Partial closure of the ground may see the spectators affected attempting to buy tickets in other parts of the stadium.

In a recent development, "This is a strong message and a sign of the FA clamping down. I hope Millwall can resolve this matter for the good of the game.".

Millwall manager Alex Neil will not be best pleased with the punishment that is likely to affect The Den's home atmosphere in their December clash against the Blades.

They have challenged for the playoffs in each of the last two seasons and even finished third last term, but are at the moment struggling in 16th place on a run of just one win in their last seven games.

Opta's supercomputer is currently predicting the Lions to finish around 15th with 60 points.

As it stands, they have a 9.56 per cent chance of making the playoffs and a 3.8 per cent chance of being relegated to League One.

Published: 05:07 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 05:13 EST, 24 November 2026.

Premier League clubs are bracing themselves for a newly introduced raid of their talent from Saudi Arabia, as the mega-money league considers relaxing spending rules.

Teams in the Saudi Pro League (SPL) are currently only allowed eight foreign players in their 25-man squads but are discussing increasing that number to 14 or even higher.

If the move is approved, it is likely to trigger a flood of cash in the market similar to the massive £765million spree in 2023 that saw the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Karim Benzema and N'Golo Kante sign for Public Investment Fund (PIF) teams.

In that 2023 window, almost half of the transfer fees received by Premier League clubs came from the SPL.

In total, 94 players were signed by Pro League clubs and the January transfer window could now follow a similar pattern.

The Saudi spending reached such astronomic levels that it eclipsed every other league in Europe aside from the Premier League.

Cristiano Ronaldo (right) and Angelo, pictured in action for Al Nassr, are among the foreign stars already plying their trade in Saudi Arabia and more will be on their way.

The supposed reason for the proposed rule change is to elevate the standard of existing Saudi players at home by raising the overall level of talent ahead of the country hosting the World Cup in 2034.

But critics argue that the new rules would only force Saudi players out of their domestic league in place of high-profile foreign recruits.

While Premier League clubs are often reluctant to allow talent to leave in January midway through the season, the fees on offer from Saudi can be eye-watering and hard to turn down.

Aston Villa sold Jhon Duran and later Ollie Watkins for a combined £115million to the SPL.

Fulham accepted £50m for Aleksandar Mitrovic, while Wolves banked £47m for Ruben Neves and Liverpool were able to recoup almost £50m for Darwin Nunez.

West Ham were able to cash in on Crysencio Summerville after relegation last term when Al Hilal bought him for £60m.

Industry observers note that would Man United consider offers for Bruno Fernandes as his contract winds down? Or will they keep the club captain to help battle relegation?

Suddenly every Premier League club recruitment department will be reassessing their squads and be keeping a close eye on the rule developments in Saudi.

Ollie Watkins moved from Aston Villa to Al Hilal and the Premier League side have recouped huge fees from the SPL in the  past.

Ivan Toney (second from left) and his Al Ahli team-mates celebrate a goal against Al Nassr.

The SPL's decision on whether to allow the increase of foreign players will be clarified before the winter window opens.

The PIF are winding down their investment in golf through LIV having invested more than £3.7billion since 2021 but their operation in football highlights no sign of slowing down.

Players weighing up a move to Saudi will perhaps have a more difficult decision than in 2023 over relocating, with conflict still affecting the country.

The Asian Cup was postponed earlier in November following a missile attack from Yemen-based Houthi rebels on Riyadh airport that killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

Security fears and geo-political uncertainty could make footballers think twice before accepting the lucrative contracts on offer in January and beyond.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 22 Nov 2026 19:53, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:44.

Galatasaray will be looking to continue their resurgence in the UEFA Champions League when they welcome Aston Villa to Rams Park on Tuesday evening, with the Turkish champions aiming to close the gap on the top eight.

The hosts sit 18th in the league-phase standings with six points from four matches, while Villa occupy sixth place on nine points and will be looking to return to winning ways after a difficult run of results.

Galatasaray head into this fixture in encouraging form after winning seven consecutive matches across all competitions, with their recent improvement helping them maintain their position at the top of the Turkish Super Lig while also strengthening their Champions League qualification prospects.

Okan Buruk's side have won their last two UCL matches, recording a 4-2 victory away to Lille before following that result with a 2-0 home triumph over VfB Stuttgart.x.

The victories helped steady the ship after Galatasaray had suffered defeats against Sporting CP and Barcelona in their opening two Champions League fixtures, leaving them with little margin for error in their pursuit of a place in the knockout stages.

They have also continued their impressive run domestically, winning their last six league matches, a run that includes a win over Fenerbahce, and most recently a 2-1 win over Samsunspor 2-1 at the weekend.

Galatasaray have also been particularly impressive at home this season, winning seven of their nine matches at Rams Park while drawing one and losing one, with Barcelona the only side to defeat them on their own turf.

They will now have the opportunity to equal their best-ever run of consecutive victories in the European Cup or Champions League by recording a third straight success.

However, their defensive record remains a concern, having conceded nine goals in their opening four Champions League matches, including four in their home defeat against Barcelona and two against Lille.

Meanwhile, Villa arrive in Istanbul having experienced a significant dip in form, with their five-game winless run following a period during which they were without defeat in eight straight games, winning seven of those matches.

Unai Emery's side began that difficult sequence with a 3-0 loss away to Bournemouth in the League Cup, before subsequently drawing 1-1 with Fulham, which preceded a disappointing result in the Champions League as they lost 3-0 away to Barcelona.

Villa then produced an entertaining but defensively concerning performance in a 4-4 draw against Manchester United, before a goalless draw with Sunderland in their last outing.

Nevertheless, Villa have made an encouraging start to their Champions League campaign, winning three of their opening four matches to collect nine points and remain among the teams occupying the automatic qualification positions.

Their European campaign has included a particularly impressive 6-0 victory against Fenerbahce, which represented their widest margin of victory in European competition against a Turkish opponent, and they will be eager to rediscover that level of performance in Istanbul.

Both teams have never met in competitive football, making Tuesday's encounter the first meeting between the sides, although the hosts have traditionally proved difficult opponents for English clubs playing in Istanbul.

English teams have failed to win in nine of their last 10 visits to Galatasaray, losing six and drawing three, while Villa have lost just once in eight European matches against Turkish opposition, winning six and drawing one.

Galatasaray are expected to be without Victor Osimhen, who underwent knee surgery after sustaining an injury during their Champions League victory over Stuttgart.

Rafael Leao is also sidelined with a muscle injury, while Roland Sallai and Ismail Jakobs are carrying fitness concerns and could miss Tuesday's encounter.

Aleksey Batrakov, who has scored four goals in the Champions League this season, three of which have been at RAMS Park, will be the man to watch in Osimhen’s absence.

Villa will be without Matty Cash, who sustained a concussion while on international duty with Poland, while Amadou Onana and Matteo Ruggeri are also expected to remain sidelined through injury.

Victor Lindelof is a doubt after missing the weekend draw against Sunderland due to illness, while Aaron Wan-Bissaka has returned from a hamstring problem and could be available for selection.

Nicolas Jackson is expected to lead the attack, with John McGinn, Emiliano Buendia and Johan Manzambi likely to provide support as Emery looks to end Villa's winless run.

Galatasaray possible starting lineup:.

Cakir; Singo, Sanchez, Bardakci, Elmali; Torreira, Lemina; Akgun, Batrakov, Yilmaz; Gul.

Aston Villa possible starting lineup:.

Suzuki; Bogarde, Harwood-Bellis, Pau Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Joao Gomes; McGinn, Buendia, Manzambi; Jackson.

Galatasaray have been in impressive form in recent weeks and their home performances should give them confidence of securing another positive result against Villa.

However, the hosts will be without several notable attacking players potentially limiting their options in the final third, and while Villa have struggled defensively during their recent winless run, they have enough in attack to play out an entertaining draw in Istanbul.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Reworded scientific phrases can thwart publishers’ plagiarism checkers, but, in many cases, the resulting combinations of words only draw more attention from scientific sleuths. Credit: Gregory Dubus/iStock via Getty.

Sources indicate that these days, I spend a lot of my time looking through published papers that I suspect are fraudulent. It is a gruelling task. But amid the tedium, there is some light relief, thanks to some hilarious phrases used by authors seeking to avoid detection by plagiarism checkers. It’s hard not to smile when ‘breast cancer’ becomes ‘bosom peril’, or a citation for ‘Baker and Logue’ become ‘Pastry Specialist and Logue’.

Industry observers note that I retired in 2022 from the University of Oxford, UK, where I worked as a developmental neuropsychologist. I now track down research fraud as part of a community of scientific sleuths. We work together to identify papers that we consider to be problematic in some way, then send the evidence to publishers or post it on PubPeer, a post-publication peer-review platform. Our aim is for the problematic papers to be investigated and, if appropriate, retracted by their publishers. But, often, publishers are slower and more recalcitrant than many sleuths would like them to be.

‘A waste of time for all of us’: caught in the crossfire of the peer-review wars.

‘A waste of time for all of us’: caught in the crossfire of the peer-review wars.

Many people blame academia’s ‘publish or perish’ research culture for the rise in problematic papers. Without a large number of publications and citations, prospects for employment, promotion and glittering prizes evaporate. Some researchers cut corners, manipulate or fabricate data, or copy the work of other scientists without citing them.

Sources indicate that the demand for desperate researchers to get their name on a publication in any journal has spawned semi-professional organizations known as paper mills. These sell authorship status, with prices that vary depending on the impact factor of the journal. Articles are typically generated using artificial-intelligence tools or plagiarized, and tend to find homes in journals that lack sufficient editorial scrutiny.

Sources indicate that one of the few amusing consequences of these developments is the phenomenon of tortured phrases, first described in 2021 by computer scientists Guillaume Cabanac and Cyril Labbé and software engineer Alexander Magazinov1. They analysed huge volumes of research literature to identify patterns. Tortured phrases arise when someone — or, in most cases, a computer — replaces words in a published article with synonyms to evade plagiarism detectors and ultimately publish the result as their own work.

Authorship for sale: Nature investigates how paper mills work.

Authorship for sale: Nature investigates how paper mills work.

Cabanac and colleagues developed a free website called the Problematic Paper Screener, which documents tortured phrases and other red flags in publications. Detection of tortured phrases has been a communal effort by research sleuths, who document specific articles with tortured phrases on PubPeer.

#175321. Liverpool vs Man Utd: Florian Wirtz leaves his mark with stunning creative display as remarkable stat emerges

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (363 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Liverpool vs Man Utd: Florian Wirtz leaves his mark with stunning creative display as remarkable stat emerges

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (363 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Saikat Mandal | 22 Nov 2026 20:04.
  • Florian Wirtz produced a stellar performance as Liverpool registered an emphatic 4-0 victory over Manchester United in Sunday's Premier League clash at Anfield.
  • Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring for the Reds after Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute, before Wirtz doubled their advantage in the first half.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 22 Nov 2026 20:04.

Florian Wirtz produced a stellar performance as Liverpool registered an emphatic 4-0 victory over Manchester United in Sunday's Premier League clash at Anfield.

Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring for the Reds after Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute, before Wirtz doubled their advantage in the first half.

Liverpool dominated possession after the interval and added two more goals, with Rio Ngumoha making history for the Reds and Victor Munoz also getting on the scoresheet.

While the Reds remain third in the Premier League table, they have closed the gap on second-placed Manchester City to one point and are seven points adrift of leaders Arsenal.

Andoni Iraola is now unbeaten in his seven Premier League matches against the Red Devils, with only legendary Liverpool manager Jurgen Klopp boasting a longer record, having gone eight games without defeat against the same opposition.

The German international came under heavy criticism from Jamie Carragher at the start of the season as he struggled to make an impact.

Wirtz has gradually rediscovered his confidence and delivered a top-class performance against the Red Devils, creating as many as 10 chances.

According to Opta Joe, Wirtz's tally was the highest by any player in a Premier League match since David Silva created 11 chances against West Bromwich Albion in March 2015.

Wirtz has now registered three goals and five assists across all competitions for the Reds this season, and those numbers are expected to rise in the coming months.

While the victory over a struggling Man Utd side reduced to 10 men may not provide a complete picture, there are signs that Liverpool's players are gradually getting to grips with Iraola's demands.

There was greater cohesion and better team chemistry throughout the contest, and the side could become even stronger once Hugo Ekitike, Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley return from injury.

Wirtz has covered considerable ground in every match, and his work rate has been second to none, but the end product had been missing.

Iraola will hope that Wirtz can build on this performance and help Liverpool reach upcoming heights as the season progresses.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Christy Grimshaw was crucial as AC Milan Women finally got back to winning ways, following what was a rather crazy first half against Sassuolo.

After two defeats and a draw, dropping points in a silly fashion against Napoli last weekend, Milan Women needed to bounce back with a win today. Thankfully, that’s exactly what they managed to do, even if it wasn’t the most controlled performance.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, just looking at the scoreline and the timing of the goals is enough to understand the nature of the game. All five goals were scored in the first half and it doesn’t end there either. All five were scored within the first 27 minutes!

According to recent reports, the veteran Grimshaw opened the scoring for the Rossonere after nine minutes, but Sassuolo found a way back into the game just two minutes later. The Scottish international decided to restore the lead just four minutes later, i.e. in the 15th minute.

Recent findings suggest that angelica Soffia then made things more comfortable with a third goal in the 24th minute, or at least so we thought. Just three minutes after that, Sassuolo scored again and thus brought some life into the game, even if Milan looked the better side.

In a recent development, suzanne Bakker’s side actually dominated possession, had more shots on target and also had a higher xG, so the win definitely feels deserved. And boy was it needed! The situation in the standings is still not great, but at least they are now four points behind the Champions League zone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alexis Pereira | 22 Nov 2026 20:19, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 20:19.

Recent findings suggest that paris Saint-Germain are reportedly one of six leading European clubs interested in Brighton and Hove Albion left-back Maxim De Cuyper, according to journalist Ekrem Konur. The Belgium international has played regularly in the Premier League since the start of 2026-27 and is under contract with the Seagulls until June 2030.

With attackers Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue both injured, PSG must decide quickly whether to make do with their current squad or use the winter transfer window to act.

In January, another area of the pitch could be strengthened by the French capital club: left-back. Lucas Digne has been limited to little playing time, and the double Champions League holders are considering a latest left-back as back-up or alternative to Nuno Mendes, at least to give the Portugal international a rest from time to time.

According to recent reports, with that in mind, the Paris hierarchy has shown interest in a Premier League left-back: Maxim De Cuyper. According to information relayed by Konur, PSG are part of a list of six renowned European clubs following the situation of the Belgian defender.

His significant playing time in England this season is one of the reasons he has attracted attention. Two Premier League giants - Arsenal and Liverpool - are also quoted as interested such as Juventus, AC Milan and AS Roma.

Latest Update: Opposition insight for Milan-Frosinone: Form, injuries, predicted XI and more

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (532 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • AC Milan are looking to make it three consecutive wins tomorrow, but a high-flying newcomer in Frosinone could make that difficult.
  • Ruben Amorim and his men have an opportunity to really establish some momentum tomorrow evening, picking up where they left off before the break.
  • Amorim even warned in his press conference that it will be a difficult one, especially since the Canarini have such a direct style.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan are looking to make it three consecutive wins tomorrow, but a high-flying newcomer in Frosinone could make that difficult.

Ruben Amorim and his men have an opportunity to really establish some momentum tomorrow evening, picking up where they left off before the break. However, it won’t be an easy game against Massimiliano Alvani’s Frosinone, who have impressed everyone so far.

Amorim even warned in his press conference that it will be a difficult one, especially since the Canarini have such a direct style.

➤ Manager: Massimiliano Alvini ➤ Form (all comps): W-D-W-W-L (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Raimondo – 8 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Kvernadze, Schmid and Ghedjemis – 4 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

According to recent reports, frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

It has been revealed that they are currently on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

Industry observers note that it’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

Sources indicate that so, what is behind this rise? As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

While collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly massive-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Recent findings suggest that moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

RB Leipzig vs Lens - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Freddie Cotton | 22 Nov 2026 20:39, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:44.
  • RB Leipzig welcome Lens to the Red Bull Arena on Tuesday evening in matchday five of the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League campaign.
  • In their previous competition outing, Die Roten Bullen suffered a narrow 3-2 defeat against Manchester City on home soil, while Les Sang et Or were thumped by Cesc Fabregas’s Como side at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Freddie Cotton | 22 Nov 2026 20:39, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:44.

RB Leipzig welcome Lens to the Red Bull Arena on Tuesday evening in matchday five of the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League campaign.

In their previous competition outing, Die Roten Bullen suffered a narrow 3-2 defeat against Manchester City on home soil, while Les Sang et Or were thumped by Cesc Fabregas’s Como side at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis.

Despite enduring a year without football on the continent last season, having finished seventh in the Bundesliga table and missed out on European competition by just one point at the end of the 2024-25 campaign, RB Leipzig will be extremely disappointed with how their return to the UEFA Champions League has panned out so far.

Following a thumping 4-1 defeat away to Como in their opening fixture, Martin Demichelis’s men did well to bounce back with victory over PSV Eindhoven in round two, but having suffered defeats against both Real Madrid and Manchester City since, Tuesday’s hosts currently sit outside the competition’s knockout-phase places with just three points.

However, they will be fairly content with the improvement to their league form, as after losing three of their first six Bundesliga matches, Die Roten Bullen have triumphed in each of their previous four to climb into the division’s Champions League qualification places.

Although they have never before faced Lens in a competitive fixture, RB Leipzig will be hopeful that they can use their upturn in domestic form to improve both their European campaign and underwhelming record against French opposition, having won just three of their prior 11 encounters with Ligue 1 sides on the continent.

After earning European qualification for the first time in three years at the end of the 2025-26 season, placing second in the Ligue 1 table and just six points behind back-to-back Champions League champions Paris Saint-Germain, Lens will also be frustrated with the start to their campaign on the continent.

Les Sang et Or got their Champions League efforts off to the perfect start as they scored twice in stoppage time to post a 3-2 victory away to Slavia Prague in their opening game, though their campaign has since unravelled as three consecutive losses have them sitting 33rd in the standings with just three points.

New boss Didier Digard will undoubtedly be concerned by his side’s losing streak in Europe, but perhaps even more alarming has been the manner in which they have been beaten, particularly in their most recent outing when they suffered the joint-biggest defeat in the competition’s history after being thumped 9-1 by newcomers Como.

Unlike their opposition, Lens have struggled in their domestic campaign too, with Les Sang et Or winning just four of their opening 11 league matches so far this season, including none of the latest three, to sit a lowly 11th in the Ligue 1 table and seven points off the automatic Champions League qualification positions.

While they have not recorded a competitive victory against German opposition since beating Bayer Leverkusen in March 2007, Lens did overcome RB Leipzig when the sides met in a pre-season friendly last year, claiming a 2-1 victory at the Stade Bollaert-Delelis.

RB Leipzig Champions League form:.

RB Leipzig form (all competitions):.

After being left out of their European roster, 32-year-old goalkeeper Leopold Zingerle will be unavailable for Tuesday’s match, while former Barcelona and Chelsea forward Marc Guiu is also missing for the hosts with a hamstring problem.

Die Roten Bullen’s only other absentee is young German midfielder Assan Ouedraogo, who suffered a shoulder injury at the end of September and has been replaced in the starting lineup by Neil El Aynaoui since.

Having netted six league goals so far this season, including one in each of his previous three outings, Demichelis will be hoping that Brazilian striker Romulo can replicate his emphatic form in the Champions League this week and score his first goal in Europe.

Much like Zingerle, Moussa Diarra and Ilan Jourdren are both missing from Lens’ Champions League squad this season, while Croatian forward Franjo Ivanovic is also ruled out against RB Leipzig due to concussion protocols.

Les Sang et Or’s list of certain absentees is rounded off by Odsonne Edouard, Jonathan Gradit, Maik Nawrocki and young Montenegrin midfielder Andrija Bulatovic, who sustained a neck issue while on international duty earlier this month.

It remains to be seen whether 33-year-old defender Ruben Aguilar will feature either, as the Frenchman reportedly continues to recover from a hamstring injury and was substituted before the hour mark against Toulouse on Saturday evening.

RB Leipzig possible starting lineup:.

Vandevoordt; Baku, Orban, Lukeba, Raum; El Aynaoui, Banzuzi; Gruda, Baumgartner, Nusa; Romulo.

Risser; Todibo, Baidoo, Chavez; Abdulhamid, Titraoui, Cuisance, Udol; Mesloub, Sotoca; Thauvin.

With both teams sitting on just three points entering the final four league-phase fixtures, Tuesday’s clash could prove pivotal if either side is to strengthen their chances of progressing to the knockout stages.

While we expect a tightly contested encounter, we think RB Leipzig will just edge their visitors to claim victory this week and are backing Demichelis’s men to move into the knockout play-off places with a valuable three points.

Bayern Munich could make a move for the AC Milan target and Club Brugge star Nicolo Tresoldi, following Harry Kane’s injury.

Tresoldi has been making waves at Club Brugge this season, scoring an impressive five goals in the Champions League, and Milan are one of several significant clubs that have been linked with him. Of course, those links are mainly fueled by the fact that the striker is a big Milan fan.

According to recent reports, as Milan fans know well after Ardon Jashari and Charles De Ketelaere, it’s notoriously difficult to negotiate with Club Brugge. That means a high offer is needed, which is something that could arrive at the Belgian side’s doorstep in January.

Recent findings suggest that according to Gazzetta dello Sport, Bayern Munich have been keeping an eye on Tresoldi for some time and initially viewed him as a potential signing for the 2027-28 season. However, due to Harry Kane’s ankle injury, they could move much earlier.

The Englishman will be out for at least three months, having had surgery this morning, and that should keep him sidelined until February/March. That puts Bayern Munich in a difficult spot, perhaps forcing them to make a move in January.

Industry observers note that club Brugge want at least €60m for their star and knowing Bayern Munich’s resources, they would be far more comfortable paying that amount than Milan. In short, Kane’s injury has not only resulted in a headache for the German side, but also for the Rossoneri.

Kroupi’s preferred destination ‘revealed’ as Bournemouth rule out January sale

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (593 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Alexis Pereira | 22 Nov 2026 21:24.
  • Recent findings suggest that barcelona may be ahead in the race for Eli Junior Kroupi, according to French outlet Foot Sur7, which reports that the 20-year-old Bournemouth forward would favour the Catalan club if he decides to leave the Premier League.
  • According to Foot Sur7, Kroupi has a special interest in playing for Barcelona, a possibility that had already been considered behind the scenes at the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Alexis Pereira | 22 Nov 2026 21:24.

Recent findings suggest that barcelona may be ahead in the race for Eli Junior Kroupi, according to French outlet Foot Sur7, which reports that the 20-year-old Bournemouth forward would favour the Catalan club if he decides to leave the Premier League. Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal are also following the striker’s situation, but for now they are stated to be behind Barcelona in the player’s preference.

According to Foot Sur7, Kroupi has a special interest in playing for Barcelona, a possibility that had already been considered behind the scenes at the club. Barcelona’s football department has followed the striker’s development since the last summer transfer window, and his name remains on sporting director Deco’s radar as an option to strengthen the attack in the coming years.

According to recent reports, the Catalan interest also gains strength from information given by David Ornstein this week. Speaking on The Athletic FC podcast, the British journalist said the Frenchman is weighing up leaving English football when he feels the time has come for a newly introduced step in his career. A departure from the Premier League would put Barcelona and PSG in a favourable position, particularly if English rivals lose ground in the race.

Sources indicate that there is still no decision on the striker’s future, however. The preference for Barcelona reported by the French press does not mean a transfer is under way or that the player has made a final choice.

In a recent development, while Barcelona appear an attractive destination, Bournemouth are set to make any short-term move difficult. The English club are not planning to lose one of their main players in the January window and consider his presence vital for their sporting goals.

The position was reinforced by boss Marco Rose, who ruled out selling the forward in January. ‘For us, it is not a plan to sell someone in January,’ Rose remarked. ‘It is not our plan and so far there are just rumours and noises.’.

Kroupi’s contract with Bournemouth also stands in the way of suitors. The striker is under contract until June 2030, which puts the Cherries in a comfortable position. With no need to release him immediately, they can set high conditions before opening talks. According to estimates in the British press, Bournemouth could ask for close to £100m to accept a transfer. That figure is a considerable barrier, particularly for Barcelona, who would need to weigh up the financial impact of an operation of this size.

The interest is not explained solely by competition among European giants. At 20, Kroupi is already one of the most talked-about young names on the market, driven by his goalscoring ability, his versatility in attack and the room for improvement he still has. Those characteristics help explain why the Frenchman fits the profile Barcelona are seeking. The Catalan hierarchy are looking for alternatives who can add quality to the attack in the medium term, and the Bournemouth player has attributes that attract Deco and other members of the football department.

PSG are also seen as a possible heavyweight rival, especially if the striker leaves English football. Arsenal are monitoring the situation, although according to Foot Sur7 they are behind Barcelona in Kroupi’s preference.

Recent findings suggest that A decision is not expected immediately. The striker intends to focus on recovering his best form this season before making any decision about a change of club, so next summer is the most likely time for a concrete assessment of his future.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The club stalwart has been put in temporary chatge at The Saffrons while the club look for a permanent replacement for Macdonald, whose axing alongside assistant Ben Davis has provoked an angry reaction from many fans and seen some players leave – includihg one who’d only rejoined the club on Friday.

The latest development at the Isthmian South East club came on Monday evening, when a club statement mentioned: “To serve for an interim period, Eastbourne Town F.C are pleased to announce the appointment of popular club stalwart Dave Winterton as First Team Manager.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

"Dave is, of course, very well known to most people in the local area for his long and distinguished playing, coaching and management career with our club, and we sincerely thank him for agreeing to take on this role.

It has been revealed that "During this time, Dave will be assisted by one of our experienced senior players, Arron Hopkinson. Our thanks also go to him.

"We hope that supporters will get behind Dave and the team during this period of transition, starting this coming Saturday away at Erith Town, whilst the search for a permanent successor to Jude Macdonald continues.”.

Dave is a second generation Winterton at Eastbourne Town – his father Derek played as a defender for the club in the 1950s.

He was club manager between June 2001 and January 2005, taking Town, who were playing in Division 2 of the Sussex League, into Division 1 and winning the Sussex Intermediate Cup. In 2020 Dave became the Goalkeeper coach for the club.

The move to make him interim boss comes after the surprise news on Saturday evening that Macdonald had been sacked with Town one off the bottom of the division but after two brighter league performances that had seen a point taken from each of two clashes with Sheppey and Whitstable.

Town’s statement on Saturday stated: “Eastbourne Town FC have today parted company with First Team Manager Jude Macdonald and Ben Davis.

"The Committee would like to place on record their sincere thanks to Jude and Ben for their hard work over the last 4½ years, where, following their arrival, they rapidly reshaped the remaining playing squad, and with some exciting new arrivals, just two years later launched an amazing mid-season recovery to storm up the SCFL Premier Division table to finish Runners-Up and then win the League Play-off Final.

"They then successfully kept the Club in the Isthmian F.L for successive seasons when largely up against many teams with much greater budgets and resources, a feat which we believe must be seen as a remarkable achievement in what is known by many to be a very tough division.

"The club wish them both all the very best for the future and thank them once again for their service during their time at The Saffrons. No further statements will be made at this time.”.

A number of Town fans have taken to social media to condemn Macdonald’s removal, calling it shocking and disgraceful.

At least a couple of players have left – including James Waters, who Macdonald had re-signed for the club only at the end of last week.

Burgess Hill Town youngsters are flying – and Byrne scores 15 goals in two games

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The team had to settle for a point after Rovers striker Matty Fanimo hit a stunner to bring the scores level at 2-2.

In isolation a point on the road is perfectly acceptable, but Mansell was feeling the effect of six league games without a win – and now 15 games without a win on grass.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

His team are quietly working their way down the table, occupying 15th place.

Buoyed by the permanent signing of winger George Vorster Hill played very well for 30 second-half minutes. Vorster put the visitors 2-1 in front on 75 minutes but then Hill seemed to go defensive and gave away a cheap free kick 25 yards out. Up stepped Fanimo to break away hearts.

Perhaps the more stinging result was a 1-0 home defeat to lowly Brentwood the previous Tuesday.

Mansell and his team held all the aces that night but for some reason couldn’t break out from a malaise. They produced one shot on target all evening. The winning goal was a very scrappy affair ending with three Hillian defenders on their backsides as Alfie Cerulli bundled home from a yard.

Mansell was quite direct in his post-match interview after that loss, saying: “Gutted, it’s a familiar pill to swallow, there wasn’t enough desire in both boxes.”.

There were raised blood pressures among fan walking away from the MTC that evening and a mixed bag of social media comments.

Away from first team matters we caught up junior section managers Tim Bourne and Ben Slade, who are passionate about providing a safe and nurturing environment for youngsters to play football.

As Tim explained: “We have over 500 players both training and playing matches across our three home facilities.”.

The MTC is a hive of activity on Saturday mornings for training and then the excellent upcoming facility The Arc and St Paul’s School host matches on Sundays.

Ben remarked: “it’s a huge operation and while Tim and I are the face, there is a large committee of passionate people all performing different tasks, this wouldn’t function without them!.”.

Sources indicate that hill’s Junior section has three teams at each age group, the youngest players are under-fives. They also facilitate coaching badges and referee courses. As Tim suggested: “It’s a well-oiled machine.”.

I ventured to the Arc last Sunday to catch up with the U13s girls team playing Fishersgate. It truly is a remarkable facility, a real mecca for youth football. Both teams put on a great performance as the visitors took a narrow victory.

The junior section is in rude health and going from strength to strength operating with the best facilities in Sussex.

Hill’s pathway section under Mansell and Berty Oliva are performing at an extraordinary level this season – the U18s and 19s Academy side continue to pick up great wins.

In a recent development, striker Bobby Byrne – son of ex-Republic of Ireland, Brighton and QPR striker John Byrne – and is making all kinds of headlines after his nine goals in one U18 Sussex Cup match. He quickly followed up with six for the U19s at Ebbsfleet.

Recent findings suggest that after the six he explained: “It’s all going very well this season. I would like to take my football to the highest level I can but first would love to play for the Hillians.”.

It has been revealed that bobby’s name is on a lot of people’s lips right now – with many calling for him to make his first team debut. It’s a certainty we will be keeping an eye on his progress.

While the club are operating at a high level right now and are always looking to enhance the profile, the vast majority of fans and connections quite rightly engage only with first team matters.

Mansell is acutely aware of this so will be looking for a win when title contenders Eastbourne Borough travel to the MTC on Saturday afternoon. Three points at this time would be huge.

Liverpool go on the hunt for a fourth win from five Champions League matches on Wednesday evening, when the Reds take on Club Brugge at the Jan Breydel Stadion.

Andoni Iraola's men have taken nine points from 12 on offer in Europe so far, good enough for eighth place in the Champions League rankings after their 3-2 loss to Fenerbahce last time out.

The Reds also return to European action on the back of a 4-0 demolition of Manchester United, rising into the top four of the Premier League table in the process.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Liverpool’s latest injury and suspension news ahead of their showdown with Club Brugge, who are just one place below Liverpool in the 36-team table courtesy of an inferior goals scored total.

Possible return date: November 29 (vs. Everton).

Cody Gakpo was a surprise absentee from the Liverpool squad against Man United, and Iraola subsequently revealed that the attacker had picked up a calf injury on Netherlands duty.

Gakpo is also expected to miss out in midweek, but there is a chance that he could recover in time for next weekend's Merseyside derby.

In a recent development, possible return date: November 25 (vs. Club Brugge).

Sunday's game against Man Utd came too soon for Ryan Gravenberch to return from a heel injury, but the midfielder might be able to make his comeback on Wednesday.

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Hugo Ekitike is making continued progress in his rehabilitation from a serious Achilles injury, but the French striker is still expected to miss the rest of 2026.

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Out for over a year with a serious knee injury, Giovanni Leoni returned to team training during the international break and is now in the "last part" of his recovery process, but a playing comeback before the Newly introduced Year is still incredibly unlikely.

Possible return date: January 2 (vs. Coventry City).

Likewise, Conor Bradley is finally back with his teammates on the training pitches after sustaining a severe knee problem in January, but it will be a few more weeks before he is considered for selection too.

Liverpool have no players suspended for this match.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Amazon rainforest plays a key part in the cycling of carbon and water on regional and global scales, and is widely viewed as a perennially evergreen ecosystem. However, writing in Nature, Song et al.1 report that there are extended periods when trees in most of the rainforest remain leafless. Known as deciduousness, this state occurs between the shedding of old leaves and the emergence and early development (flushing) of fresh ones. The authors also found that hydroclimatic conditions such as annual rainfall have a more crucial role in determining this pattern of leaf behaviour than do soil properties and light availability. The seasonal variation in tropical leaf cover and photosynthetic activity in the Amazon observed by the authors is less pronounced than that seen for broadleaf trees in temperate and boreal climate zones.
