📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Milan will return to action on Sunday evening, hoping to pick up where they left off before the international break with a strong performance against Frosinone.
  • Industry observers note that if we look at the league, it has been a very decent start to the season for Ruben Amorim and his men.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Milan will return to action on Sunday evening, hoping to pick up where they left off before the international break with a strong performance against Frosinone.

Industry observers note that if we look at the league, it has been a very decent start to the season for Ruben Amorim and his men. However, they are yet to win three games on the trot, so tomorrow’s encounter is a fantastic chance for them to really show their worth.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, it won’t be easy, though. Amorim said during his press conference that it’s hard to identify the movement patterns of Frosinone, who certainly have the ability to make life difficult for the Rossoneri.

Game date: Sunday, November 22 Kick-off time: 18:00 (CET) Venue: San Siro Referee: Luca Pairetto (VAR: Pezzuto).

Recent findings suggest that some good news arrived on Saturday morning as Strahinja Pavlovic was deemed fit enough to be called up for the game. It’s not certain whether he will start or not, but Amorim at least mentioned that he’s happy to have the Serbian and ‘his fire’ back.

It has been revealed that A few days ago, it was also confirmed that Mike Maignan will be at the manager’s disposal despite the injury scare with France. Of course, it’s not all perfect on the injury front as Matteo Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze are still sidelined.

According to recent reports, anyway, moving on to the predicted starting eleven, it was initially thought that Amorim would field the same one as we saw against Genoa. However, he made it very clear during the presser that Musah won’t play as a left-back, so there will indeed be some changes.

Sources indicate that according to the latest reports, the American will still start but in midfield instead, allowing Adrien Rabiot to have a slightly more advanced role. It also means that Davide Bartesaghi will come into the eleven, presently ahead of Pervis Estupinan in the race.

Alphadjo Cisse has been in red-hot form lately but it seems Amorim wants to manage expectations a little, with the youngster tipped to start on the bench. Christian Pulisic should thus have a role on the flank as opposed to in the centre, although one would imagine everything will be a bit fluid.

It’s no surprise to see that Goncalo Ramos should start up front, but of course, he will need to get going with the goalscoring sooner rather than later. Francesco Camarda is knocking on the door, as is Cisse who has been tested in that role before.

Predicted Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Musah, Modric, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

Predicted bench: Torriani, P. Terracciano, F. Terracciano, Pavlovic, Vladimirov, Estupinan, Jashari, Comotto, Hutchinson, Cisse, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Gabbia, Tomori, Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers and Chukwueze.

In a recent development, frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

They are presently on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

It’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

So, what is behind this rise? As pointed out by Gazzetta dello Sport, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

While collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly big-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Recent findings suggest that moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

This fixture has only been played six times, but even with such a small sample size, it’s clear that Milan are the favourites with four wins and two draws so far. They have won the last three as well, spread across the 2023-24 and 2018-19 seasons.

Sources indicate that that said, the most recent encounter was a dramatic one, if you like. Olivier Giroud opened the scoring for Milan away from home but then Frosinone scored twice. Thanks to goals from Matteo Gabbia and Luka Jovic, the Rossoneri were able to turn it back in their favour.

In a recent development, the last time at San Siro, meanwhile, it was a great 3-1 win as Jovic, Pulisic and Tomori found the back of the net. Most of you will remember the American’s goal, as it was Maignan who assisted him with a fantastic pass.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in all six previous meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W4 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

Industry observers note that ➤ Milan have scored at least three goals in four of their six Serie A matches against Frosinone, producing 15 goals overall, an average of 2.5 per game. Only against Pescara (2.9) have they recorded a higher average, among the opponents they have faced on at least five occasions (2.5 also against Casale and Messina).

➤ Frosinone have won six games this season, drawing two and losing three. Only three newly promoted teams in the last 40 years have recorded more wins in their first 12 Serie A games of the season: Bari in 1994/95 (seven), Chievo in 2001/02 (seven), and Hellas Verona in 2013/14 (seven).

➤ Milan have won four of their last five league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in consecutive Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

➤ Although Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their five away games this season (W1 D2), they have won just two of their last 27 away games in Serie A (including previous participations), with 10 draws and 15 defeats.

Industry observers note that ➤ Milan have failed to win four of their last seven Serie A games played after the international break (D2 L2). On the other hand, Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their last five top-flight matches immediately following Italy matches (W2 D1).

It has been revealed that ➤ Frosinone have attempted the most counterattacks from advantageous situations in Serie A this season: 22, almost double the number of any other team. On the other hand, Milan are the only team that haven’t allowed a single counterattack when trailing in the current campaign.

According to recent reports, ➤ Only Juventus (79) have attempted more long-range shots than Frosinone (77) this season. On the other hand, Milan are the team that have attempted the fewest shots from outside the area (30) and the one that have conceded the most shots from outside the area in relation to the total conceded, 44%.

Recent findings suggest that ➤ Adrien Rabiot has earned the most points for his team from direct goal contributions this season, having scored 10 goals and assisted four times. In the most recent matchday, he became the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal in six consecutive league appearances since Kaká in 2004 (who managed seven).

➤ Only Matías Soulé (80) has been involved in more sequences ending with a shot than Giacomo Calò (76) in this Serie A. The Frosinone player has scored five goals in the current campaign and only one midfielder has scored more goals in the first 12 matchdays in the top flight for a newly promoted team in the three points for a win era: Hidetoshi Nakata with Perugia in 1998/99 (six).

Sources indicate that since Frosinone like to play on the counterattacks, one player who I think could be crucial for Milan is Musah. As he’s set to start in midfield and not at left-back, the feeling is that his main role will be to prevent the opponents from having too much open space on the counter.

Sources indicate that further up the pitch, I’m excited to see Moreira. He got himself a goal in Belgium’s win over Italy and he has looked a lot better on the right flank ever since the derby performance. He can definitely make the difference with his skill.

Sources indicate that as for Frosinone, it’s obvious that Calo is the man whom Milan will want to stop. He likes to dictate the play and if he’s allowed too much time on the ball, identifying his teammates in good positions, then there could be trouble for the Rossoneri.

It will also be interesting to see if Birigilea can fill the shoes of Raimondo. He bagged a brace against Lecce but in the last two games, he failed to find the back of the net. He will surely be keen to get back on target.

A lot of people are expecting this to be a high-scoring affair and that’s a very reasonable take, given how both teams play. That remarked, I think this could be one where Milan actually get their defence in order and don’t concede, even if that might be a somewhat optimistic prediction.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, this Brighton and Hove Albion title challenge – as it must now be classed – flies in the face of the saying that money always talks in football. Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching financial rules and also fielded the most expensive midfield in Premier League history here, yet the match-winners cost a fraction in comparison.

Industry observers note that looking at Brighton’s winning goal, it was created by a cross that flashed across the City goal from Diego Gómez, an £11m signing who was playing in Major League Soccer in the United States not so long ago. Maxim de Cuyper, a £17.5m arrival from Club Brugge, was credited with the assist after Yasin Ayari tapped in.

Ayari cost £3.5m from Swedish club AIK and scored in the 5-0 wins over Coventry and Palace, and now has this winner to add to his collection. The 23-year-old is another example of Brighton polishing these gems and putting them together in a team that can win against any opponent in the Premier League.

It could keep them at the top end of the table for a good while longer. They have already shown they can defeat Arsenal in a one-off match and they look to have the ingredients to stay the pace with them. In Fabian Hürzeler they have one of the brightest young coaches in the Premier League and he has a squad that are all on the same page.

According to recent reports, leicester upset the odds 10 years ago with a settled team, while this Brighton team has a deeper squad. When the substitutes came on in the second half, they slotted into a well-rehearsed system.

Recent findings suggest that “We faced adversity. There was a little bit of luck but in the end they deserved it because they worked hard for it,” remarked Hürzeler. “I want players who want to compete, to dominate. They all have the winning mentality inside of them. These kinds of performances are not about one or two players, everyone has to stick together.”.

While Hürzeler was reluctant to name individual performers, Dutch goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen was another key player in this win. He kept out Iliman Ndiaye and repelled Erling Haaland, who lost a physical battle with Lewis Dunk. “You’re going down with the Palace,” chanted the jubilant Brighton fans, with City now losing two Premier League games in a row.

Sources indicate that city head coach Enzo Maresca will be content with the number of chances his team created but there must be concerns at the other end. He tried a change of formula, dropping Marc Guéhi to the bench for the first time this season, yet his team were still prone to individual errors.

“We are the second team in scoring in the Premier League. We are scoring goals but in this moment we are conceding silly goals. We can avoid that,” Maresca stated. His team have conceded 10 goals in their last six games, which is not the foundation of a title challenge, even if City have been stacking up points.

There were some signs they could all play together, although City looked more dangerous when Rayan Cherki came off the bench to break up the trio.

Pascal Gross cost a nominal fee when he returned to Brighton but his hard work and intelligent passing means Brighton can control periods of the game even against the very best.

According to recent reports, the goal came when Brighton switched play from a free-kick, although City thought Anderson was victim rather than perpetrator. Former Inter Miami winger Gómez provided the cross that opened up City, with Gianluigi Donnarumma guilty of not coming out to claim the ball, then Matheus Nunes slipped at the vital moment.

“Unfortunately it is happening for our players but I think it is part of the game, part of football, it happens many times against us, we need to analyse and understand what we can do better,” Maresca added. City also felt Dunk used his arm to block the ball in the penalty area, although no spot-kick was given.

It was a sweet goal by Ayari, who had missed a penalty in the shoot-out last week when the teams played in the EFL Cup. Brighton stayed in Manchester after the defeat, masterminding a win that means they have now defeated all of the traditional heavyweight teams in the Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that “I wasn’t aware of that. For me it’s more crucial, not about history, it’s about giving something back to the supporters. They’ve spent a lot of time and money,” Hürzeler said.

“We’ll take it game by game. See what happens because we have loads of games. Just focussing every day on what’s ahead of us and the job we have. We will continue to do that and see where it leaves us at the end of the season. We are happy with the way we are playing - not just the results but the way we are playing too. We have to continue to develop that style and ruthlessness and we can do great things.”.

In City-related matters, Jack Grealish is battling for his future next season and faces becoming the Premier League’s most high-profile free agent following his breach of discipline at Everton.

The 31-year-old, who became the first £100m signing by an English club in 2021, is out of contract in eight months and his hopes of staying on Merseyside took a hit when the club decided he would not play in the Carabao Cup win over Newcastle.

While City head coach Enzo Maresca described Grealish as “a good boy with a massive heart”, there are no signs of him getting a contract extension at the Etihad Stadium after being loaned out in the last two seasons.

Grealish is expected to be fined by Everton for an unauthorised absence from training and it is unclear when he will be back in David Moyes’ squad, with the club facing Newcastle again on Monday in the Premier League.

He had started the previous four matches and a return to playing regularly will be the key to securing a club next season.

“It is not correct to talk about Jack as he is an Everton player and I don’t have all the information,” remarked Maresca, who worked with Grealish when he was in Pep Guardiola’s backroom staff. “I still think he is a good guy, a good boy with a massive heart.”.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this Saturday’s 3pm Premier League kick-offs.

The most eye-catching fixture sees Manchester City host Brighton & Hove Albion for the second time this week at the Etihad Stadium. On Wednesday evening in the League Cup, Enzo Maresca’s side squeezed past Fabian Hurzeler’s men on penalties (4-3) thanks to second-choice goalkeeper Geronimo Rulli’s heroics after drawing 2-2 in normal time.

Nevertheless, despite this disappointment and the 2-0 loss to Liverpool last weekend, Brighton sit third in the league, just five points behind table-toppers Man City, who suffered their first domestic defeat against Aston Villa seven days ago, which ended their perfect record in this season’s Premier League.

Recent findings suggest that speaking in his Friday press conference, Maresca stated: “I think we’re going in the right direction. I said in the last press conference, after so many years to change manager and many players it takes time to compete again and in this moment we are competing.

“We changed many players and the manager but good thing about the club is we are competing in all the competitions and we know it takes time when you make this many changes but in this moment, we continue in the same way.”.

In a recent development, following a rocky start to the campaign, high-flying Bournemouth have won their previous five matches in all competitions without conceding, beating the likes of AC Milan, Manchester United and Aston Villa by three-goal margins. Blackwell, 67, was appointed manager until the end of the season on Thursday (November 19).

And the 67-year-old has made a strong impression with the Crawley faithful so far.

“They were the 12th man today,” he stated, after the game. “Because when we needed them, they gave us that vocal support that really, really helped us.

Recent findings suggest that “They were that loud at times, they [the players] couldn't hear what I was trying to shout across the pitch. So, listen, long may that continue, but we've given them something to shout [about] – that's the thing.

“The fans will respond if we do our job as professional people, footballers, and they've done their job today and the fans have responded.

“And I made this comment in our previous meetings that we've had – if we're going to get out of the trouble we're in, it's all of us. Me, the players, the staff, the owners, the fans – it's us. It's Crawley Town Football Club, that's who'll get out of this.”.

Will Davies’ 79th-minute goal for the Cod Army made it a nervy finish to the contest.

The Broadfield erupted in a mixture of elation and relief at full time – the latter particularly understandable given the difficult start to the season.

Blackwell stated: “If you don’t win, going into late November and you haven’t won at home yet, I think everyone was nervous. Because to win the game is a rarity – that can’t be right.

Industry observers note that “We've got to make sure that becomes the norm. Your home form is what normally keeps you in the league. So, our home form has got to improve. As I said, I'm under no illusion here. We know it's going to be a tough one, but we know that if we work like that, and we've had 21 days since the last game, and let me tell you, they have worked very, very hard.

In a recent development, “And today you saw a lot more powerful running, a lot more aggression in tackles and overall a good shape to the team. So, a lot of pluses today, but as I said to the boys in there after the game, ‘we've won, but that wasn't right and that wasn't right’, having complimented them on how well they did. So, there's still things to improve on and we'll keep doing that.”.

The Us started the second half well, forcing Heath on to the backfoot but failing to create any clear-cut chances.

Their most dangerous tactic seemed to be launching long throws into the Bears penalty area where they met by a solid-looking Broadbridge Heath defence marshalled by Lewis Hyde and supported by his protégé Jay Richardson.

But the Bears doubled their lead on the hour mark when Young received the ball wide on the right of the Hastings penalty area and forced his way forward, where he was challenged by a defender – bringing the Heath player crashing to the ground.

The match referee had no doubt about it being a foul, pointing immediately to the penalty spot, and MoM Young picked himself up, dusted himself down and hammered the spot kick into the back of the net for his second of the afternoon, helping his side to a 2-0 win.

The victory saw Broadbridge Heath move into one of the play-off places in seventh – just one point behind Hastings United.

Fixtures continue to come thick and fast with the Bears travelling to second-placed Erith Town on Tuesday evening before returning home again on Saturday to face leaders Faversham Town.

By Anthony Nolan | 22 Nov 2026 23:17, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 05:02.

Mauricio Pochettino will take charge of his first Champions League game in the Manchester United dugout on Wednesday, when the team travel to face Sporting Lisbon in Portugal.

The Red Devils were thrashed 4-0 by Liverpool on Sunday, and are looking to Europe for a reprieve from their domestic woes.

Pochettino started Patrick Dorgu and brought Harry Maguire on as a substitute at Anfield, though he remains without a significant number of players ahead of this midweek clash.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up all of Man United's injury and suspension news ahead of their Champions League showdown with Sporting.

Sources indicate that possible return date: December 2 (vs. Newcastle United).

Midfielder Carlos Baleba was forced off with a hamstring injury during United's 3-2 win over Roma last time out in the Champions League, and is eyeing a return to action in early December.

It has been revealed that possible return date: December 2 (vs. Newcastle).

Marcus Rashford has been out of action since a lingering hip issue spread to his groin last month, and he is unlikely to feature on Wednesday after missing the Liverpool game.

Possible return date: November 25 (vs. Sporting Lisbon).

Left-back Luke Shaw has been sidelined since United's 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur on October 10, and though he missed the defeat to Liverpool, his return to training suggests he could be in with a chance of making the squad on Wednesday.

Striker Benjamin Sesko has been dealing with a recurring shin injury that he initially developed towards the end of the 2025-26 campaign, and while he was thought to be closing in on a return this autumn, his recovery timeline has reportedly slipped closer to the start of 2027.

Defensive midfielder Manuel Ugarte suffered a serious knee injury during World Cup 2026, and is likely to be sidelined until the spring after undergoing surgery and rehabilitation.

Versatile forward Matheus Cunha was the hero of United's win against Roma, but he was sent off late in the game after receiving a second yellow card for his celebrations.

Gary Neville slaps himself in the FACE in bizarre on-air moment after Man United's humiliation at Anfield - weeks after claiming his old club are 'in a better place' than Liverpool

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (935 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 04:43 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Gary Neville showcased the dramatic decline of Manchester United this season as he bizarrely slapped himself in the face on Sky Sports after his former side's 4-0, 10-man, defeat to Liverpool at Anfield.
  • Neville's dramatic example of Man United's lack of hunger and sharpness came in stark contrast to his pre-season proclamations for the side, when he informed his co-pundit Jamie Carragher that he believed that then-manager Michael Carrick's starting XI was stronger than Liverpool's after a summer recruitment drive.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:43 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

Gary Neville showcased the dramatic decline of Manchester United this season as he bizarrely slapped himself in the face on Sky Sports after his former side's 4-0, 10-man, defeat to Liverpool at Anfield.

Neville's dramatic example of Man United's lack of hunger and sharpness came in stark contrast to his pre-season proclamations for the side, when he informed his co-pundit Jamie Carragher that he believed that then-manager Michael Carrick's starting XI was stronger than Liverpool's after a summer recruitment drive.

Instead, Man United saw their numbers reduced inside the opening stages of the game after a reckless challenge by Leny Yoro, and 2-0 down after 13 minutes, with the club legend resorting to drastic methods to convey the side's weaknesses.

Of his old club's defenders, he said: 'I never see any of them on their toes, alert, looking like they've got something fixed in here', before pointing to his head.

'I never see any of them look like that,' he added. 'They look like that -'.

Neville then stared into the middle distance for a few moments to share the blankness he sees on the faces of the back line, before spitting: 'Wake up!'.

Gary Neville took to slapping himself to convey the lack of focus he sees in Man United's stars.

The club legend had previously tipped his old side to have a stronger XI than Liverpool's.

But when the two teams met at Anfield, Man United were left woefully exposed after going down to 10 men.

The Overlap broadcaster then slapped his own face a number of times repeating 'wake up!' before adding: 'You play for Man United'.

The gesture left Carragher in stitches, with the Anfield icon collapsing onto the sofa in hysterics - although less impressed with Roy Keane, who displayed his usual sangfroid.

So tickled by the moment was the former Liverpool star that he later changed his profile picture on social media site X to a still image of Neville's hand catching his face.

Neville had more sharp criticism for Man United's defensive selection assessing the inclusion of Matthijs de Ligt in the starting line-up.

The Dutch defender has been out of Premier League action for 51 weeks after suffering a back injury, but was named by Mauricio Pochettino in his first-ever XI.

Recent findings suggest that 'I have a lot of sympathy for him,' Neville admitted. 'It's like playing football after having six pints. It's a strange feeling.

'I have a lot of sympathy for him, it's alarming to watch.'.

Less sympathy for Man United's players came from Keane, who attacked the team - and Neville and Carragher - after the heavy defeat at Anfield confirmed the club's worst start in over 53 years.

The firebrand midfielder was on his usual caustic form as he assessed the damage, hitting out at those who might have accepted the score line, having feared a greater deficit.

'If I hear that one more time from the lads in the commentary that 4-0 is not too bad when you're down to 10 men - has a team ever got a result with 10 men before?' Keane remarked immediately after the final whistle. 'It can be done.

'I thought United were desperate. I thought they were so bad and everyone and Nev, who played for Man United saying 4-0 ain't bad.'.

Sources indicate that '(The red card) doesn't help but you're telling me they couldn't have done better? They lost 4-0 with 10 men, that's not too bad? Has a team ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality - I can't believe what I'm hearing from people.

'You played for the club, saying 4-0 isn't too bad. Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish. Liverpool were excellent, but how easy did United make it for them? I can't believe what I'm watching sometimes.

'This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers.

It has been revealed that 'When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making? Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying 4 is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'.

The difference between the two teams felt a far cry from Neville's late-summer prediction, when he told Carragher that he had greater hopes for Carrick and Man United over incoming manager Andoni Iraola at Liverpool.

According to recent reports, 'I think Manchester United are presently in a better place than Liverpool,' Neville stated in August. 'Would you agree?'.

Carragher remarked that he did not, and will have been confident in his assessment on Sunday night.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that roffey faced clear table toppers Haywards Heath, at the Fusion Aviation Stadium on Saturday, determined to gain revenge for the narrow, and perhaps undeserved, loss at Hanbury Park earlier in the season.
  • In the second minute Jordan Mase went down the left then cut in and switched the ball across the box to Luke Harrison whose shot took a slight deflection, taking the pace off it and Ethan McGrath in the Blues goal saved.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that roffey faced clear table toppers Haywards Heath, at the Fusion Aviation Stadium on Saturday, determined to gain revenge for the narrow, and perhaps undeserved, loss at Hanbury Park earlier in the season. However, in the end, despite having 14 attempts on goal with 6 on target, it was the visitors who took the points with two clinical finishes from their four on target efforts and two off target.

In the second minute Jordan Mase went down the left then cut in and switched the ball across the box to Luke Harrison whose shot took a slight deflection, taking the pace off it and Ethan McGrath in the Blues goal saved. In the fourth minute Mase again advanced before squaring it, this time to Stan Berry who hit a fierce drive just past the right-hand post, with McGrath probably covering it. Two minutes later Tom Caplin fed Moyo on the right and after his first cross was blocked at the near post he found Caplin 12 yards out but his shot although right in the corner, lacked the pace to beat McGrath.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The Boars continued to dominate possession and after a quarter of an hour, Mase set the ball back for Charlie Gibson to fire over from twenty yards. Next a Gibson corner was deflected up in the air by a defender and Pat Gibs headed it back into the danger area where Berry controlled the ball in the air before hitting a spectacular bicycle shot a foot over the bar. Gibson hit his hot wide at the end of quick break and Berry hit the side netting after good work from Harrison and Callum Kilkenny.

Heath had their first attempt on goal after twenty-two minutes when Sonny Causton was played through, but with defenders converging, hit his shot from the edge of the box straight at Charlie Burton. Back came Roffey and Teddy Wood put a twenty yarder narrowly past the right-hand post. Heath responded with Mark Goldson getting behind the defence, but Pat Gibbs held him up and the Boars got men back with his attempt ending tamely in Burton’s arms. Goldson had another chance when the ball was switched from the right, but he sliced his shot wide.

The breakthrough came on thirty-three minutes when a Roffey attack broke down, and the ball was rapidly transferred to Josh Wright who had kept himself onside. Burton advanced to push him wide but Callum Kilkenny who had sprinted back went over the top of the outstretched keeper and Wright managed to squeeze the ball in at the far post despite the desperate efforts of Jack Meeres on the line. Wood replied with a shot that was saved comfortably by McGrath. After all that action the half ended quietly with the visitors having the advantage.

Roffey had the first attempt on goal after the break with Moyo’s shot being taken above his head by McGrath. The game became much more contained with Heath happy to close Roffey down and maintain their lead. The next significant action didn’t come until thirteen minutes before time when Roffey lost possession in their own area but forced Harry Shooman to shoot over. Roffey were still very much in the game, but this changed on eighty minutes as they threw men forward, the hosts were caught on the break and Wright held off Meeres and rolled the ball past Burton to double the lead. Roffey wouldn’t give up but Heath were now able to sit back and soak up the pressure. Gibsons free kick hit the wall and deflected for a corner which was cleared. As stoppage time approached the Boars had a great chance to stay in the game when Caplin spread the play out to Harrison whose cross picked out the same player, unmarked ten yards out, but he scuffed his shot and McGrath saved. There was still time for Moyo to force a save out of McGrath at the near post and the same player hit a shot wide but unfortunately time had run out for the Boars. The table toppers had shown a clinical edge and managed their way to the three points.

Roffey are still very much in the fight for a top five place and it looks like that could be between eight or nine teams and the Boars next match is away to one of them, Hassocks who sit two places above the Boars, on December 1st.

Roffey: Burton, Harrison, Gibson, Napper, Gibbs(Moyo), Meeres, Wood, Mase, Berry(Allen), Caplin, Kilkenny(Hoarty). Subs: Pearse, Skerry.

Eastbourne United and Guernsey show why they are promotion contenders

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (574 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A 4-1 defeat left Guernsey smarting and United in a very good position in second place in the SCFL Premier.
  • Since then, the Green Lions have been on an unbeaten run, making themselves genuine play-off contenders along with United.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 4-1 defeat left Guernsey smarting and United in a very good position in second place in the SCFL Premier.

Since then, the Green Lions have been on an unbeaten run, making themselves genuine play-off contenders along with United. It was obvious from the moment they arrived at the Oval that they would only be happy with all three points, preferably by at least the same scoreline.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The early encounters went to United, and with just seven minutes on the clock James Jull shot home, only for the linesman to raise his flag for offside to howls of derision from the home support.

Guernsey started to make their mark with a couple of runs from Charlton Gauvain, but the visitors also left their mark on United’s players, collecting two yellow cards.

Hull went very close with an acrobatic scissor kick, and Joe Overy continued to needle away down the left wing, Charlie Ball forcing the keeper into a good save from one of Overy’s low crosses.

In first half added time, Guernsey took the lead with a fine shot from range beating Alieu Secka.

United were unperturbed and Rhyle Ovenden was unfortunate not to even it up straight after the break, his free kick just scraping the top of the crossbar.

On the hour Hull was replaced by Callum Barlow, before the increasingly confident Ovenden had a shot well saved by the Lions keeper.

Five minutes later, Barlow’s lightning-fast cross found Overy, who turned and slotted home well for 1-1. Overy rarely misses an attempt in the area, and Guernsey looked crestfallen.

There was a third and a fourth yellow card for Guernsey, who were pondering returning with only a point, when Ball broke past the defences and slotted home with an inch perfect side foot to make it 2-1 to United to the joy of the crowd, and despair of the islanders.

Rather than crumble, it galvanised Guernsey, and the United lead only lasted four minutes as Gauvain made it 2-2. Now it was a real blood and thunder contest, both teams showing exactly why they are in the top four, Secka made a wonderful save to keep it equal, Ball and Barlow both trying out the away keeper, but it remained 2-2.

After months out injured, the home crowd were delighted to see – on 85 minutes – Mason Creese come on, replacing Ball, and Freddie Jones took up position on the other flank replacing Overy.

Sources indicate that both added even more pace, and despite the cold, the crowd were heating up – while Guernsey overheated as they collected a fifth yellow in what was never a nasty encounter. As the final whistle went both teams were treated to an ovation as they left the field. This is the sort of fare non-league crowds absolutely love - hard tackling, fast attacking, stout defending and not a player from either side faking injury to get an opponent booked.

Both teams should be in the play-offs - one of them could be champions, time will tell.

According to recent reports, next up for United, this Saturday, is a home game with an improving Forest Row, who will be desperate for the points to help them out of the drop zone. It’s a 3pm kick-off at the Oval.

Man United transfer news: Calvin Bassey gives "negotiations" revision as relegation battle makes Mauricio Pochettino desperate

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (468 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Nolan | 22 Nov 2026 23:34, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 01:54.
  • Fulham defender Calvin Bassey has confirmed he is in negotiations to extend his contract despite interest from Manchester United this January.
  • The Red Devils were resoundingly beaten by Liverpool on Sunday, losing 4-0 at Anfield, with defender Leny Yoro receiving an early red card.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 22 Nov 2026 23:34, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 01:54.

Fulham defender Calvin Bassey has confirmed he is in negotiations to extend his contract despite interest from Manchester United this January.

The Red Devils were resoundingly beaten by Liverpool on Sunday, losing 4-0 at Anfield, with defender Leny Yoro receiving an early red card.

Mauricio Pochettino has only been leading the club since Wednesday, but he will already be aware of the need to address the team's defensive frailties, especially as they are 19th in the Premier League table with just eight points after 11 matchweeks.

The Red Devils have been linked with centre-back Bassey, but the defender confirmed that he is in discussions to extend his deal with Fulham, telling TNT Sports: "We’re still negotiating, we’re still talking and obviously it’s an amazing place to be.

I’ve settled in nicely and the manager has put a lot of faith and trust in me. So, it’s nice to be here and hopefully we will see what happens with the negotiations.".

Bassey's current deal is set to expire in 2027, though Fulham have an option to extend his stay by a year, so news that the 26-year-old is hopeful of further extending his time at Craven Cottage will come as a blow to Pochettino.

“Just proud of the boys today, you know how hard it is to play here” Calvin Bassey and David Affengruber reflect on a huge point for Fulham away at the Etihad ? ? Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/Szb8cvHyJ6.

Bassey is a strong channel defender and is much more athletic than United's current options at the back, something that has been a major issue this season.

Harry Maguire is now 33 and his mobility problems have only worsened as he has aged, while Lisandro Martinez has never been suited to playing in an aggressive, high-pressing system.

Yoro is young enough to contribute in the coming seasons, but he has not developed since signing for the club in July 2024.

The Premier League is the most physically and mentally demanding league in the world, and signing someone with experience of the top flight would be hugely beneficial.

The reservations that some have at the club about Bassey's place in the XI in the years to come should not matter given the real threat of relegation.

United would have ended Sunday bottom of the league had Crystal Palace beaten Coventry City on Saturday, and the fixture schedule does not get any easier for the Red Devils.

With games against Brentford, Newcastle United, Coventry, Palace, Arsenal, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland to come before the end of the year, Pochettino's side cannot afford to drop many points if they wish to avoid the one-point gap to safety increasing.

Scotland’s World Cup award can be game-changing for the nation

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scotland captain Caroline Weir says the country being named as a host nation for the 2035 Women’s World Cup is a “pivotal moment” for the sport.

The United Kingdom’s four-nation bid was given the official seal of approval in a vote by acclamation at an Extraordinary FIFA Congress on Monday, having been the sole valid bid in contention for the event.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Nineteen stadiums are proposed, with 14 in England, one in Northern Ireland, two in Scotland and two in Wales in a tournament which will feature 48 teams.

Recent findings suggest that while the 2022 European Championships were held in England, Scotland has never hosted a major women’s football event. Hampden Park in Glasgow (capacity 52,032) and Hibs’ Easter Road in Edinburgh (capacity 20,093) are Scotland’s Candidate Stadiums and would stage at least group-stage matches. Weir feels that having the competition on Scotland’s doorstep will show youngsters in this country that “anything is possible”.

Industry observers note that midfielder Weir, who at the moment plays for Lyon and has won 122 caps for Scotland, said: “Hosting the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup in the UK is a pivotal moment for women’s football in this country. Playing at the 2019 Women’s World Cup in France was an incredible moment in my career, so knowing that the next generation of Scottish players will have the chance to experience that on home soil is so special.

“The women's game in Scotland has so much potential and this tournament is a real opportunity to drive momentum and help take it to another level both nationally and internationally.

“For young girls and boys across the country, seeing the best players in the world right on their doorstep will show them that anything is possible.

“We’re so proud to play our part in welcoming the world in 2035 and I know I speak on behalf of all of the players and staff when I say that we are ready to rise to the challenge and help deliver a truly memorable, world-class tournament.”.

In a recent development, scottish Football chief executive Ian Maxwell hailed the decision to award the event to the UK. “Securing the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup alongside our Home Nations partners is a momentous milestone for Scottish football,” he stated. “Scotland has a proud footballing heritage and a rapidly growing women’s game, and welcoming the world to Barclays Hampden and Easter Road will turbo-charge the progress we have made across our grassroots, domestic, and international game.

In a recent development, “This tournament will be the single-biggest sporting event ever staged in the UK, and our ambition goes far beyond the matches themselves. It gives us a powerful platform to inspire participation in a new generation of girls and women across Scotland, empower more female leaders and match officials and deliver a sustainable commercial and community legacy for many years to come.”.

It will be the first time that Easter Road, the home of Hibs, has been selected to host a major international event and the club say they are hugely excited at the prospect.

Hibs Women’s head coach Joelle Murray noted: “This is fantastic news for women's football in Scotland and something we should all be extremely excited about.

Industry observers note that “To welcome the best players in the world to Easter Road would be incredibly special and provide a brilliant opportunity to showcase the women's game. It would also give young girls across the country the chance to experience a World Cup on their doorstep and to see what is possible to achieve through football.

According to recent reports, “Having played and coached at Easter Road throughout my career, it holds a very special place in my heart. To see it named as a Candidate Stadium for a Women's World Cup is a hugely proud moment for me, and the opportunity to inspire the next generation makes it even more exciting.”.

Hibs chief executive Dan Barnett added: “The inclusion of Easter Road as a Candidate Stadium for the 2035 FIFA Women's World Cup is fantastic news for the Club and the City of Edinburgh.

"This is something we've been working hard on for several months, with various positive discussions with the Scottish FA and key stakeholders. In recent years, we have been delighted to host Scotland Women's National Team matches at Easter Road, so to be named as a Candidate Stadium for the finals in 2035 is a huge honour.

“To have the opportunity to showcase our stadium on the world's biggest stage would be an immensely proud moment for the Club. It presents a unique opportunity to welcome tens of thousands of supporters from across the world to Edinburgh and create a lasting legacy for the women's game.

"We're excited by the next steps and the prospect of working alongside the Scottish FA, the City of Edinburgh Council and our partners to help bring this opportunity to life.”.

According to recent reports, the bid team projected the tournament would attract 3.5 billion viewers worldwide, and that 4.5 million tickets would be sold. FIFA’s evaluation of the bid, published earlier this month, rated it 4.3 out of five.

The tournament will feature 48 nations and 104 matches across 39 days, with the final host cities and stadiums to be confirmed by FIFA in due course.

Brighton were frustrated after failing to make their first-half dominance count, but midfielder Andres is looking ahead to the visit of Romanian league leaders Universitatea Craiova in the Uefa Conference League.

The Spaniard has made an impressive impact since his £18m summer arrival, featuring 10 times for Albion in all competitions, including eight Premier League appearances. He has also scored and provided an assist.

Andres believes the squad must learn from the setback at Hull rather than allow it to affect their confidence.

“What is good for us, we have another game on Thursday,” he said.

“We're already focused on that, and I think we need to focus on ourselves, keep training, see what we did wrong today, learn, and of course go again because this is football and sometimes you lose.

“I think the team spirit and team effort is not going to go down, so we will come back again.”.

The 21-year-old acknowledged the cost of Brighton's missed chances against a Hull side who indicated their quality late on.

“This is the Premier League, no? If you don't use the chances you have, and then you give this kind of team the opportunity to beat you, that is what they got.”.

Andres added that Albion must accept the defeat, learn from it and move forward promptly.

Thursday's meeting with Craiova offers an immediate opportunity for Brighton to respond.

“We will recover from this and bounce back again,” he said.

Brighton then return to Premier League action this Sunday against Newcastle at the Amex Stadium.

Brighton were made to pay for their wastefulness when Oli McBurnie struck twice in stoppage time, following Costinha's late dismissal for a second yellow card.

And former Manchester United captain Keane believes Hull deserve enormous credit for their fighting spirit after sustained pressure from Albion.

"It's a mad game. The sending off had a big impact. Brighton were desperately trying to win the game, and you have to give credit to them, but they left spaces and gaps," Keane told Sky Sports.

"It's brilliant from Hull, great fighting spirit and a bit of quality. Great composure from McBurnie. You think McBurnie has missed the opportunity, but what a huge goal.".

Keane was also keen to highlight the contribution of Hull goalkeeper Tzolakis, who produced a string of outstanding saves to frustrate Fabian Hurzeler's side.

"Instead of being critical of Brighton, you have to give credit to the goalkeeper," he added.

"They might not have Brighton's quality, but they showed great fighting spirit, composure, and stayed in the game; you have to give them huge credit for that.".

The result leaves Brighton second in the Premier League table with 22 points from 11 matches, while Hull climb to 11th with 14 points.

Jamie McGrath has dismissed the idea Hibs players do not enjoying playing at home as they bid to halt a 10-game run without victory at Easter Road in the William Hill Premiership.

The Hibees have not won a league game on their own turf since defeating Kilmarnock 3-0 in early April and their supporters turned on them during a grim 4-0 defeat by Dundee United on Saturday that left them second bottom of the table.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

If they fail to beat Dundee on Tuesday, the winless streak in Leith will extend beyond the eight-month mark.

“I don’t know,” stated midfielder McGrath on why he thought they were struggling for results at Easter Road. “Personally, I always like playing at home. I love the pitch, I love the stadium. It’s a massive open pitch, which I think should suit us. But for whatever reason, so far this season we haven’t been able to capitalise on playing at home.

In a recent development, “It’s hard to put your finger on one certain thing. Maybe just being more decisive in both boxes or probably conceding goals at crucial times in the game, like after five minutes on Saturday, we just give ourselves a bit of a mountain to climb. It’s hard to put your finger on it, but it’s something that we’re trying to put right.”.

After a difficult start to the season which resulted in Marink Reedijk replacing David Gray as manager in late September, it looked like Hibs had turned the corner when they followed up a rousing victory over city rivals Hearts in the Premier Sports Cup semi-final with a 4-0 win at Aberdeen in their last game before the international break.

Recent findings suggest that mcGrath, therefore, is hopeful Saturday’s aberration will prove a blip. “We’ve been on a decent run the last month and probably the international break came at a tricky time for us,” noted the Republic of Ireland international. Or not a tricky time, but we were just kind of building momentum and had two good wins back-to-back against two good teams.

“It’s frustrating not to build on that, but hopefully we can put Saturday down to a bad day and get back on track.”.

McGrath is unfazed by Hibs being 11th in the table as he senses a chance to change that with three matches in the space of nine days against other sides in the bottom six.

“It’s not something that we’re concerned about at the minute,” he said. “It’s obviously not where we want to be.

“We want to try to get closer to that top six and this two-week period is quite crucial in terms of there being nine points in the next week up for grabs. If you put a little run together, you can boost yourself right up the league.

“It’s just about finding that consistency to hopefully propel us up the league.”.

The Brazilian played a role in Jude Bellingham’s equaliser and Carlos Espi’s winner and will now get the opportunity to impress from the start, as Los Blancos look to maintain their perfect record in the 2026-27 Champions League.

In addition to Vinicius's inclusion, there could also be further alterations in the attacking trio behind Kylian Mbappe, with Spanish media reporting that Mourinho may decide to rest Arda Guler and Bellingham as he looks to protect his stars amid a busy schedule.

Such a decision could open the door for Brahim Diaz to operate as the number 10, while Yan Diomande may move over to the right flank after starting on the left wing on Saturday.

Aurelien Tchouameni, who withdrew from the France squad earlier this month due to injury, was deemed fit enough to make the bench at the weekend and is an option to start in central midfield alongside Eduardo Camavinga.

Marc Cucurella will take Alvaro Carreras's spot at left-back, while Federico Valverde is likely to get the nod over Trent Alexander-Arnold and ex-PSV defender Denzel Dumfries on the right side of the backline.

Eder Militao could feature in central defence after starting the 3-2 win over AEK Athens in Real Madrid's most recent Champions League game.

The Brazilian played alongside Antonio Rudiger in Greece, and they could resume their partnership if Mourinho decides to rest Dean Huijsen and Ibrahima Konate.

Courtois; Valverde, Militao, Rudiger, Cucurella; Tchouameni, Camavinga; Diomande, Diaz, Vinicius; Mbappe.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brighton should have right-back Joao Costinha available for Thursday's Uefa Conference League clash despite his late dismissal against Hull City.

The Portuguese defender was sent off in the 89th minute of Sunday's 2-0 Premier League defeat at the MKM Stadium after receiving a second yellow card for his foul on Sorba Thomas.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The dismissal proved costly for Fabian Hurzeler's second placed side, who conceded twice in stoppage time through Oli McBurnie.

However, Costinha will escape a European suspension because his red card was received in a domestic competition.

Under FA rules, receiving a second caution in the same match carries an automatic one-game suspension, which only kicks in for the domestic league and domestic cups.

That means Costinha will miss this Sunday’s match Premier League clash against Newcastle at the Amex Stadium but should be available for Albion’s trip to Bournemouth on December 2.

Uefa operates separately to the Premier League which means Costinha can feature against Universitatea Craiova at the Amex Stadium on Thursday.

Hurzeler admitted the sending-off had a significant impact on Brighton's defeat but insisted the referee was not responsible for the result.

"Of course when you are one man down, the red card plays a role," he stated.

The German added: "For 65 minutes we highlighted a good performance then we dropped our intensity, levels and standards.

Industry observers note that "In the Premier League they can punish you especially after a red card. Overall a frustrating afternoon, a frustrating game but we have to keep going.".

Hurzeler also refused to blame referee Peter Bankes, saying: "The referee wasn't the reason why we lost.".
